newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins edge down on light profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins edge down on light profit-taking.

text.p: Russian MinFin bonds edged down on Thursday as Western buyers took profits after a week of all-time record highs.
But dealers said further losses were unlikely ahead of Friday's U.S. June Producer Price Index data, which some said were expected to be positive for the bond market.

"Profit-taking started as there have been many people in long positions," National Reserve Bank dealer Andrei Ivanov-Golitsyn said. "But they were unwilling to sell awaiting further rise but the dip started on client selling."

Dealers forecast MinFin prices were unlikely to fall more than 0.25 points ahead of the U.S. June Producer Price Index due out on Friday. Economists forecast PPI would be unchanged, which would be a market-friendly factor.
MinFins, along with other emerging debt, are sensitive to any news suggesting a change in U.S. interest rates and U.S. Treasury bond prices.
"Selling was seen mainly on the London side," one dealer said. "Russian banks either preferred to stay sidelined and wait for higher levels, or were closing positions if they had them."
